https://drive.google.com/file/d/1O2QeARutrNf7wZA1GExioWlnS9XMLJ07/view?usp=sharing

The rest of this proof-of-achievement individually addresses the milestone outputs, acceptance criteria, and evidence of completion.
Please note that we have evolved Hydrozoa’s design from the tentative outline in the original Statement of Milestones on August 13, 2024. The new design provides the same functionality in a simpler, clearer, and more efficient way.
• Output 1. Specification document for on-chain validators and minting policies.
All on-chain validators and minting policies are described in Chapters 1 and 2 of the technical specification. These chapters also describe the transactions that interact with these validators and minting policies.
Relative to the original Statement of Milestones:
- The “head minting policy” is now a simple native script requiring unanimous consent from the peers. See the first paragraph of Chapter 1.
- The “head state validator” is now split into two scripts: a native script that controls the head’s treasury while peers are responsive on L2 and a Plutus-based script that controls it if peers stop responding on L2. See sections 1.1 and 2.4.
- The “deposit validator” is now implemented as the same native script, paired with a mechanism to obtain post-dated refund transactions signed by the peers ahead of time via the L2 consensus protocol. Doing so ensures that deposits are never stranded in the head when the peers stop responding on L2. See sections 1.3, 1.4, and 5.5.

Milestone Output 1–2, Acceptance Criterion 1–2, Evidence of Completion 3. We have implemented the basic L1 state model, on-chain code, and offchain code of the Hydrozoa protocol:
・L1 state model (spec §1–2). The Hydrozoa protocol has two operating regimes, each with a distinct L1 state model.
・Multisig regime
・In this regime, all funds and state of the Hydrozoa head are stored at a single native script address that allows the head peers to do anything they please, as long as they all agree. The Hydrozoa L2 consensus protocol is responsible for generating state transitions and obtaining the peers’ unanimous consent in this regime.
・The L1 state in this regime consists of the following utxos:
・The treasury utxo contains the head’s funds.
・The deposit utxos contain funds and instructions for user deposits awaiting absorption into the head.
・The rollout utxos contain funds that a settlement transaction pays out in-aggregate, deferring the individual withdrawal payouts to subsequent rollout transactions. They are produced when settlement transactions cannot fulfill all the withdrawals of an L2 block in a single Cardano L1 transaction.

ms.report:
We are proud to submit the proof of achievement for the final milestone of this project!
Over the course of Fund 12, we specified, implemented, and tested the Hydrozoa protocol — a lightweight, scalable Layer 2 for Cardano — across five milestones. This final milestone delivers the last protocol operations (dynamic head membership, plus arbitrary-size settlement and evacuation), finalizes the documentation and test suite, demonstrates a full multi-participant head on a public Cardano testnet, and closes out the project with a public report and video.
Evolution since Milestone 4. Since Milestone 4 (delivered August 2025), the Hydrozoa effort converged with a companion protocol, Gummiworm, and the two are now developed as a single unified design. The Gummiworm whitepaper is now the project's authoritative design document, superseding the frozen Hydrozoa specification. This evolution is described more fully in the whitepaper article Hydrozoa and Gummiworm: Co-evolution and convergence. Throughout this document we map the Fund 12 milestone vocabulary onto the current Gummiworm codebase.
Terminology change. The 2024 Statement of Milestones used earlier names for several concepts. In current (Gummiworm) terms:
・Head peers (and the new coil peers) were called "participants".
・Blocks (now grouped into block stacks) were called "snapshots".
・Deposits and withdrawals were called "commits" and "decommits".
・The multisig and rule-based regimes were called the "open" and "halted" head states.
・Fallback, dispute resolution, and evacuation were called "halting", "contestation", and "dissolution".
・The settlement / rollout / finalization sequences were called "AlgoSettle" (settlement-transaction trees).
・The KZG evacuation commitments and proofs were called "AlgoDissolveCert" (dissolution-certificate trees).
